assessments.reasoning: The HTTPS response returned LICENSE from the exact jpr5/ngrep commit path named in the citation. The returned body counted 3,393 UTF-8 bytes and 69 LF bytes, and its reported SHA-256 matched the claim's pinned digest. The prefix starts with Jordan Ritter's 2017 attribution, includes the grant and five restrictions, and ends with the final disclaimer period at offset 1838 and LF at offset 1839. Three further LFs occupy offsets 1840–1842. The tcpkill/dsniff introduction starts at offset 1843 and leads into Dug Song's separate attribution, redistribution conditions, and disclaimer. Similar disclaimer language recurs in that second notice, so the attribution and intervening notice boundary matter. This source establishes the publisher side of the comparison. [Pinned ngrep LICENSE](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jpr5/ngrep/351ac491358f89a7860bbbe9963cb4bc7d60000f/LICENSE)

The detail record at the specified SPDX data commit identifies licenseId as ngrep and names it ngrep License. The original JSON counted 8,703 bytes. After decoding JSON escapes, including the disclaimer apostrophes, licenseText counted 1,840 UTF-8 bytes with 38 LFs and matched the publisher prefix exactly. The record's cross-reference points to the mutable master LICENSE and reports match as the string false. That adverse metadata provides no commit-specific corroboration and does not identify the text range tested. The bounded comparison was made using the decoded field, with no whitespace or punctuation normalization. This record supports the identifier and decoded-text bindings at the pinned data commit, with the release label unverified. [Pinned SPDX detail record](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spdx/license-list-data/31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48/json/details/ngrep.json)

The standalone ngrep.txt at the same SPDX data commit counted 1,840 UTF-8 bytes, with 38 LFs and no CR bytes. Its complete body matched both publisher bytes [0,1840) and decoded licenseText byte for byte, including the final LF. The standalone file ends at that boundary. The separator and second notice in the publisher file lie beyond it. This source supports the standalone-text binding at the pinned data commit and supplies no release label. [Pinned SPDX standalone text](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/spdx/license-list-data/31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48/text/ngrep.txt)

limitations: The publisher LICENSE contains a further 1,553 bytes covering separator whitespace and a distinct tcpkill/dsniff notice attributed to Dug Song. The correspondence covers only the first 1,840 bytes.

The publisher URL identifies the requested commit. The three originals provide no independent commit history or tag evidence tying the publisher file to a named ngrep release or tying the SPDX data commit to 3.29.0.
The policy commit and bundle SHA-256 were supplied as assessment context. The permitted sources do not independently verify them.
The comparison establishes documentary correspondence only. Legal equivalence, rights for other works, reuse, and installation require separate evidence.
reasoning: The three originals establish the exact byte correspondence and bind it to the SPDX identifier ngrep at data commit 31ba1a50e5397e00a304dbadc76531740e89ee48. The publisher prefix, SPDX standalone text, and decoded SPDX licenseText are identical across all 1,840 UTF-8 bytes, including 38 LF bytes and the final LF. The originals use commit-pinned paths, but neither SPDX artifact identifies that data commit as release 3.29.0. The affirmative claim includes that release designation, which remains unverified.
